## Shared context (verbatim, immutable)

# Review Context (generated by llm-review-bench)

This file is immutable for this run. Every reviewer receives the same case facts and no
access to gold labels, other reviewer output, or adjudication records.

## 1. Objective

docs: bound llm-ledger archiving to sanitized audit records

MUST: archive review runs as audit records only — exclude logs/, agent-output/,
and snapshot/, which carry raw model output that the benchmark security
boundary forbids committing, or a nested worktree — and archive the matching
.review-benchmark/gold/<run-id>/ so report and rescore still recompute from the
archive.
MUST: stage and push from a dedicated ledger worktree after fetching
origin/llm-ledger, creating the branch from an orphan root only when absent;
on non-fast-forward rejection rebase onto the fetched tip and retry; remove
the delivery worktree only once the pushed tip contains the topic.
MUST NOT: commit raw reviewer logs or agent output to any branch, or drop the
gold tree from the archive.

Addresses the first two review rounds: raw-log security conflict, missing
gold, missing append protocol, git-ignored staging, and the omitted
ledger-checkout step.

summary: The archive layout correctly places benchmark runs and gold beneath a topic-specific root, but the new policy still leaks refactoring-review logs and conflicts with the benchmark's promised durable raw-log audit trail after delivery cleanup.

findings.title: Refactoring-review logs bypass the archive exclusions
findings.trigger: A code delivery runs refactoring-review and then archives its `.agents/reviews/<run>` directory as instructed.
findings.consequence: Raw detector stdout, stderr, and last-message files are copied to and committed on `llm-ledger`, violating the stated security boundary against committing reviewer logs or agent output.
findings.evidence: The new procedure copies the entire refactoring-review run at `.agents/skills/project-delivery/references/workflow.md:23-24`, but excludes only directories named `logs/`, `agent-output/`, and `snapshot/` at :24-26. Refactoring-review instead writes `agents/<id>/attempt-N.stdout.log`, `attempt-N.stderr.log`, and `attempt-N.last-message.txt` in `scripts/refactoring-review.py:751-760`, then reads that output into its findings at :798-801.
findings.suggestedFix: Define a sanitized allowlist for `.agents/reviews` archives, or exclude the entire `agents/` subtree and retain only vetted plan, merged-result, metrics, rules, and report artifacts before staging the refactoring-review archive.

findings.title: Sanitized delivery archive contradicts the durable raw-log audit contract
findings.trigger: After a completed benchmark run is archived and its delivery worktree is removed, a maintainer later needs the original stdout or stderr to audit a reviewer result or revisit parser behavior.
findings.consequence: The durable `llm-ledger` archive lacks the raw logs that the benchmark contract says remain auditable across sessions, so the promised raw-output audit and parser re-investigation cannot be performed after cleanup.
findings.evidence: The new policy excludes `logs/` and removes the source worktree in `design/llm-review-benchmark.md:317-321` and `.agents/skills/project-delivery/references/workflow.md:19-28`. The same live contract still requires every reviewer's raw responses and logs to be auditable afterwards at `design/llm-review-benchmark.md:30-33` and says run directories keep logs auditable across sessions at :113-114. The CLI documentation also states that raw logs are retained so parsing can be revisited in `tools/llm-review-bench/README.md:354-355`.
findings.suggestedFix: Explicitly redefine the durable audit record as the structured, sanitized artifacts and update the raw-log retention and parser-debugging promises accordingly, or specify an approved access-controlled non-Git retention path for raw logs.
